name: Heritage Speakers and Family Languages
title: Heritage Speakers and Family Languages
answer: This idea is about using AI to support students who speak a language other than English at home, especially when their speaking and listening are stronger than their reading and writing. It matters because these heritage speakers often do not fit neatly into beginner or advanced language classes, and their family languages can become a resource for social studies projects. Teachers use AI to create materials at the right level and to help with transcription and translation, while people check the language and meaning.

crumbs.name: Social Studies, Civics, and World Languages

sections.body: Many students come to school already speaking a family language other than English. They may understand and speak that language well but have had few chances to read and write it. Standard language classes can place them poorly because they are neither beginners nor fully advanced. AI can help teachers create reading and writing materials at a level that fits their actual skills. The teacher still checks that the language matches the variety the student's family speaks.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In social studies, a student can interview a grandparent about migration, work, or community life in the family language. AI transcription and translation can support the project, and the student checks and corrects the result. The student then translates and shares the story with the class. This honors the family's knowledge and builds the student's skills in both languages. The text does not give grade bands for this practice, so it can be adapted to the age and language level of the student.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The supplied text gives no evidence label, study, figure, or finding for this idea. It describes a teaching practice and a project design rather than citing research. So this idea rests on practice rather than research as presented here. Any claims about its effectiveness would need evidence beyond this text.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Teachers should be careful when translating family stories. Machine translation can miss tone, humor, and cultural meaning, and a family's story deserves care. Where possible, the student or a fluent speaker should review any translation before it is shared. The goal is to carry the family's voice faithfully, not to reduce or distort it. Decisions about accuracy, cultural meaning, and whether a translation is ready to share stay with a person.
